rubric.name: literature-host-interfaces milestone close
criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if the delivered code does not do what the plan's goal predicates and criteria claim, or a claimed result is not supported by the code, tests and records at this commit. "No concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.

The spec is the approved plan (r6) with its close amendments A1 to A3 in section 11; rows tagged (o) are owner rulings and are not re-argued. Check whether each goal predicate and each criterion LH1-C1 to LH4-C7 is met by the code in src/gnd/examples/literature/reading.py, depth.py, assurance_report.py and assertion_admission.py and by the tests in tests/test_lh1_reading_host.py, tests/test_lh2_reading_replay.py, tests/test_lh3_admission_shape.py and tests/test_lh4_admission_rules.py, as close-results.md claims.
Check the delta: is every listed departure true of the code, justified, and recorded where it says; is any departure from the plan missing from it?

The phase records (.gnd-planning/milestones/literature-host-interfaces/002-phase-LH1.md to 005-phase-LH4.md) say that some last review repairs were read by no reviewer (59fd62f0, 9df661c8, f718b572, 4428a24d). Read that code especially.

Look for an input the change claims to handle that gets a wrong result or escapes as an exception other than the refusals each API names: hostile profiles, rosters, producer answers, run folders, shapes, rules and populations.

Every regular expression, string split, slice and special-case branch the milestone added handles the whole class of input it is given, not only the examples in the tests and fixtures, and none reads structured text that a parser or an existing reader in this repository already reads.
Every concern's evidence must quote one of the three named artifacts; cite code and tests by path and line in the observation.
